headline: Statistical methods link non-coding variants, methylation, and gene-environment effects
label: Statistical Methods In Omics
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair higher-powered omics statistics with large-scale resources, including 173,303 Pakistan Genome Resource exomes and genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is statistical methodology for omics data that increases power or interpretability while controlling error. SMS calibrates the composite null for FDR control in high-dimensional mediation analysis, and SAGELD extends genome-wide gene-environment testing to longitudinal traits while controlling sample relatedness, reporting 10- to 10,000-fold speedups. targPred uses genomic regulatory blocks to link non-coding GWAS SNPs to distal target genes. A network-based DNA methylation clock built from age-correlated blood CpGs outperforms five established clocks, and a locus-specific method infers X-chromosome escape from inactivation as a function of phenotype or covariates. BMI-by-SNP interaction eQTLs show that interaction-based expression models replicate more disease genes than SNP-only models. The Pakistan Genome Resource catalogues homozygous loss-of-function variants in 6,476 genes. What is new is the shift toward models that encode interaction, mediation, and network context explicitly.
